title: LLVM IR Deep Dive
concept: A comprehensive deep dive into LLVM IR — understanding SSA form, phi nodes, basic blocks, and how the IR represents all program constructs.
why: LLVM IR is the universal language of the XIOM backend. Mastering it enables you to understand optimization, debug performance, and even write compiler passes.
theory:
## LLVM IR: The Complete Picture

### SSA (Static Single Assignment)

Every variable is assigned EXACTLY once:

```llvm
; BAD (not SSA):
%x = add i32 1, 2
%x = add i32 %x, 3  ; Second assignment — not allowed!

; GOOD (SSA):
%x1 = add i32 1, 2
%x2 = add i32 %x1, 3  ; New name for new value
```

### Basic Blocks

A basic block is a straight-line sequence of instructions with:
- One entry point (first instruction)
- One exit point (terminator instruction)

```llvm
define i64 @max(i64 %a, i64 %b) {
entry:                          ; Basic Block 1
  %cmp = icmp sgt i64 %a, %b
  br i1 %cmp, label %a_bigger, label %b_bigger

a_bigger:                       ; Basic Block 2
  ret i64 %a

b_bigger:                       ; Basic Block 3
  ret i64 %b
}
```

### Control Flow Graph (CFG)

```
      entry
     /     \
    v       v
a_bigger  b_bigger
    |       |
    v       v
  (return) (return)
```

### Phi Nodes

Phi nodes merge values from different incoming paths:

```llvm
define i64 @abs(i64 %x) {
entry:
  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %x, 0
  br i1 %cmp, label %negate, label %done

negate:
  %neg = sub i64 0, %x
  br label %done

done:
  %result = phi i64 [%x, %entry], [%neg, %negate]
  ret i64 %result
}
```

### Types in LLVM IR

| LLVM Type | XIOM Equivalent |
|-----------|----------------|
| i1 | Bool |
| i8 | Byte (Int8) |
| i32 | Int (Int32) |
| i64 | Long (Int64) |
| float | Float32 |
| double | Float64 |
| ptr | *T (pointer) |
| {ty1, ty2} | Struct |
| [N x ty] | Array |
| <N x ty> | Vector (SIMD) |

### Memory Operations

```llvm
; Allocate stack space
%ptr = alloca i64

; Store value
store i64 42, i64* %ptr

; Load value
%val = load i64, i64* %ptr

; Pointer arithmetic (struct field access)
%field_ptr = getelementptr {i64, double}, {i64, double}* %struct_ptr, i32 0, i32 1
```

### Function Calls

```llvm
; Call a function
%result = call i64 @add(i64 %a, i64 %b)

; Indirect call (function pointer)
%result = call i64 %fn_ptr(i64 %a, i64 %b)
```

xiom build --emit-ir main.xi
tips: Every LLVM function starts with 'entry' block — it's the only block without predecessors
Phi nodes are the ONLY way to get different values based on control flow in SSA
alloca creates stack space, load/store transfer values — this is how mutable XIOM variables become SSA IR
Use `xiom build --emit-ir` and read the output — it's the best way to understand compilation
common_mistakes: Trying to reassign SSA variables — use new names for new values
Confusing phi nodes with regular instructions — phis must be at the START of a block
Not understanding that alloca/load/store pattern is how mutable variables are represented in SSA
